To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

thermoplastic elastomer materials are suitable for the production of heart assist devices and that the use of these materials is associated with the risk of thrombosis, destruction of cellular elements and immune response.
the polymeric materials, especially thermoplastic elastomer, are the most promising materials for the fabrication of heart assist devices.

the thermoplastic elastomer materials, mainly polyurethanes and polyesters, can be successfully used for the construction of heart assist devices, but their application is limited due to the lack of knowledge on the long-term behavior of the materials in vivo, as well as their limited availability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structure and properties of thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs) and thermoplastic polyesters (TPEs).
the synthesis and characterization of new polymeric materials with desired properties for application in the biomedical industry.

the development of new materials for cardiovascular support system, which would be characterized by improved biocompatibility and hemocompatibility, better resistance to mechanical stresses, and would be easier to process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the materials for VADs are still not perfect and that the development of new materials is still a challenge.
the development of new biomaterials is a very important and challenging task, which requires a great deal of research and a lot of effort.
polymeric materials are a promising alternative for heart assist devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the materials for VADs should be developed in a multidisciplinary approach involving the expertise of material scientists, engineers, and medical professionals.
polyurethane and its derivatives are the best choice for the construction of heart assist devices.
the development of novel materials for cardiovascular support is still in its infancy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is still a need to develop a material that would satisfy all the requirements for VAD construction.
polyurethane elastomers are the most promising construction material for VADs, due to their high mechanical properties, good chemical stability and biocompatibility.

the development and improvement of new materials and the application of new technologies in the design of cardiovascular assist devices will be crucial for the development of the next generation of these systems.
